assessment_kind_note: Estimates the LIKELIHOOD of diagnosed cardiac disease. Module 8's RULE_HEART_DISEASE_RISK_FACTORS emits the same condition string from a RISK-FACTOR COUNT. Both are legitimate and they are not the same quantity; the predictor stamps metadata.assessment_kind on every decision so Modules 16/17 can fuse them without conflating burden with probability.

dataset.outcome_definition: Positive if a doctor ever diagnosed ANY of coronary heart disease, heart attack, angina or congestive heart failure. Negative only if all four were answered 'no'. Stroke is excluded as cerebrovascular.

excluded_columns.Systolic_BP / Diastolic_BP: VaidyaAI collects no blood pressure; a model leaning on them could never be fed at inference.
excluded_columns.Vitamin_D / Vitamin_B12: DIETARY INTAKE (mcg/day), not the serum levels VaidyaAI's identically-named features hold. Different quantity.
excluded_columns.C_Reactive: No CRP entry in feature_catalog.py; VaidyaAI cannot supply it.
excluded_columns.nutrition block: Dietary recall; VaidyaAI has no dietary features.
excluded_columns.Stroke: Cerebrovascular, not the cardiac condition Module 8 names.

dataset.resampling: none -- class weights only, no SMOTE, no oversampling

cholesterol_semantics: CONTINUOUS total cholesterol in mg/dL -- NOT v1's 1/2/3 NCEP band. Keeping the real number is worth +0.024 ROC-AUC over banding it, measured on this dataset. app/ml/heart.py's cholesterol_band() is not used by this artifact.
variant_policy: ONE variant, `all`. NHANES-CVD carries no smoking column, so a with_smoking pipeline would be the without_smoking pipeline renamed -- a variant claiming an input it never saw. v1's two variants differed by 0.002 ROC-AUC.
threshold_basis: 75th and 90th percentiles of the OUT-OF-FOLD score distribution. At 9% prevalence a 0.5 cut-off would call almost nobody positive.
feature_importance_caveat: A whole-dataset ranking. It says what the model relies on across the cohort, NOT why any one patient was scored as they were.

comparison_to_v1.note: The two numbers are computed on DIFFERENT populations and DIFFERENT outcome definitions, so this is not a like-for-like contest and should not be quoted as one. The claim being made is narrower and still worth making: on the same three inputs, a nationally representative cohort with a stated diagnostic outcome supports a materially better discriminator than cardio_train did, and does so at a realistic 9% prevalence rather than a constructed 50%.

honest_read: Held-out ROC-AUC near 0.81 on age, BMI and total cholesterol alone, at a realistic 9% prevalence. That is a usable coarse discriminator and nothing more: PR-AUC around 0.30 against a 0.09 baseline means most people it ranks highly will still not have heart disease, so a high score is a reason to discuss testing with a clinician, never a finding. The outcome is SELF-REPORTED physician diagnosis, which misses undiagnosed disease and therefore under-counts exactly the people a screening tool most wants to find. The strongest known predictor of cardiovascular disease -- blood pressure -- is still absent from VaidyaAI entirely, and adding a systolic reading to Module 2 remains the single highest-value change available to this predictor.
